choice_b: Adjustment only needs to be checked once per year
choice_c: Brake adjustment never changes once set at the factory
choice_d: Only the parking brake requires adjustment checks
explanation: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly, especially when they are hot; therefore, check brake adjustment often.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.5 - Brake Fading or Failure

question: On a long and/or steep downgrade, what role do the brakes play according to the manual?
choice_a: The use of brakes is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine
choice_b: The brakes should be used exclusively, with the engine in neutral
choice_c: The parking brake should be used continuously
choice_d: The engine braking effect should never be relied upon
explanation: The use of brakes on a long and/or steep downgrade is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.6 - Proper Braking Technique

question: Once in the proper low gear on a downgrade, how hard should you apply the brakes?
choice_a: As hard as physically possible at all times
choice_b: Just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown
choice_c: Only using the modulating control valve, never the pedal
choice_d: Only in short taps under one second
explanation: Apply the brakes just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.6 - Proper Braking Technique

question: When should you release the brakes during the proper downgrade braking technique, and about how long should the application last?
choice_a: When speed has been reduced to approximately five mph below your 'safe' speed; application should last about three seconds
choice_b: When speed reaches zero; application should last ten seconds
choice_c: Only when the low air pressure warning activates
choice_d: Never release until reaching the bottom of the grade
explanation: When your speed has been reduced to approximately five mph below your 'safe' speed, release the brakes; this application should last about three seconds.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.6 - Proper Braking Technique

question: In the manual's example, if your 'safe' speed is 40 mph, at what speed do you apply the brakes and to what speed do you reduce before releasing?
choice_a: Apply at 40 mph, reduce to 35 mph, then release
choice_b: Apply at 45 mph, reduce to 30 mph, then release
choice_c: Apply at 35 mph, reduce to 40 mph, then release
choice_d: Apply at 50 mph, reduce to 45 mph, then release
explanation: If your safe speed is 40 mph, you would not apply the brakes until your speed reaches 40 mph, apply hard enough to gradually reduce your speed to 35 mph, then release.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.6 - Proper Braking Technique

question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning comes on while driving?
choice_a: Stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible
choice_b: Increase speed to reach the destination before pressure drops further
choice_c: Switch to the modulating control valve and continue at highway speed
choice_d: Ignore it unless the buzzer also sounds
explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible; there might be an air leak in the system.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.7 - Low Air Pressure

question: Why can a heavily loaded vehicle take a long distance to stop once the spring brakes come on due to low air pressure?
choice_a: Because the spring brakes do not work on all axles
choice_b: Because heavier vehicles have weaker springs
choice_c: Because the alcohol evaporator interferes with braking
choice_d: Because the governor cuts out completely
explanation: A heavily loaded vehicle will take a long distance to stop because the spring brakes do not work on all axles.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.7 - Low Air Pressure

question: What risk do lightly loaded vehicles or vehicles on slippery roads face when the spring brakes come on?
choice_a: They may skid out of control
choice_b: They automatically stop faster with no risk
choice_c: They lose all braking ability entirely
choice_d: The stop light switch fails
explanation: Lightly loaded vehicles or vehicles on slippery roads may skid out of control when the spring brakes come on.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.7 - Low Air Pressure

question: Why is it safer to stop while there is still enough air in the tanks to use the foot brakes?
choice_a: Because controlled braking is only possible while enough air remains in the air tanks
choice_b: Because the parking brake cannot function without air
choice_c: Because the governor requires manual air pressure to reset
choice_d: Because the stop light switch needs air pressure to work at all times
explanation: Controlled braking is possible only while enough air remains in the air tanks; it is much safer to stop while there is enough air in the tanks to use the foot brakes.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.7 - Low Air Pressure

question: What color and shape is the parking brake control knob on newer vehicles, as described in Section 5.4.8?
choice_a: A yellow, diamond-shaped knob labeled 'parking brakes'
choice_b: A round blue knob
choice_c: A red square button
choice_d: A green triangular lever
explanation: The control will be a yellow, diamond-shaped knob labeled 'parking brakes' on newer vehicles.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes

question: Why shouldn't you use the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot, such as from just coming down a steep grade?
choice_a: If used while very hot, they can be damaged by the heat
choice_b: Hot brakes automatically disengage the parking control
choice_c: It will trigger the ABS malfunction lamp
choice_d: It will overfill the alcohol evaporator
explanation: Don't use the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot; if they are used while they are very hot, they can be damaged by the heat.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes

question: What can happen if you use the parking brakes when the brakes are very wet in freezing temperatures?
choice_a: They can freeze so the vehicle cannot move
choice_b: They will dry out faster and work better
choice_c: The alcohol evaporator will automatically compensate
choice_d: Nothing; wet brakes are unaffected by freezing
explanation: If they are used in freezing temperatures when the brakes are very wet, they can freeze so the vehicle cannot move.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes

question: What should you do instead of using the parking brake if the brakes are hot or wet, according to the manual?
choice_a: Use wheel chocks on a level surface, and if wet, use the brakes lightly while driving in a low gear to heat and dry them
choice_b: Disconnect the trailer air lines and leave the vehicle unattended
choice_c: Immediately drain all air tanks
choice_d: Rev the engine at full throttle to dry the brakes quickly
explanation: Use wheel chocks on a level surface to hold the vehicle; let hot brakes cool before using the parking brakes, and if the brakes are wet, use the brakes lightly while driving in a low gear to heat and dry them.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes

question: What must you never do when leaving your vehicle, according to the manual?
choice_a: Leave it unattended without applying the parking brakes or chocking the wheels
choice_b: Leave the low air pressure warning light on
choice_c: Leave the modulating control valve engaged
choice_d: Leave the alcohol evaporator container open
explanation: Never leave your vehicle unattended without applying the parking brakes or chocking the wheels; your vehicle might roll away and cause injury and damage.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes

question: If a vehicle does not have automatic air tank drains, how often should the air tanks be drained?
choice_a: At the end of each working day
choice_b: Once a month
choice_c: Only during scheduled maintenance visits
choice_d: Once every 45 seconds while idling
explanation: If your vehicle does not have automatic air tank drains, drain your air tanks at the end of each working day to remove moisture and oil.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes
